# From slate marginal value to bid control: policy weights and constraints

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/recommendation/slates-business-value.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-04 · 38 topic entries / 6 representative comparisons

CDM distills teacher choices balancing relevance and redundancy. SORT-Gen estimates prefix-conditioned marginal slate value. PRL-PUTS sweeps multi-objective policy weights. Primal-Dual Decoding updates multipliers using constraint slack during decoding. They change list context, utility modeling, policy selection, and constraint control respectively. More diversity or improvement on one metric is not an overall win. RLBP applies multi-objective governance to daily PID parameter choices, whose BU/CPC rewards and actions are not per-item slate utility.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### The same score may answer different levels of questions

CDM's MMR teacher discounts redundancy with selected items. SORT-Gen puts the slate prefix into the predictor so expected clicks and transactions vary by prefix. PRL-PUTS instead picks differently weighted policies above Q estimates. That does not give each item a universally correct fixed score. Separate utility estimation, candidate search, and policy governance.

Sources: [Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en.md) · [A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao](../../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en.md) · [A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems](../../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en.md)

### Multi-objective preferences cannot replace feasibility checks

PRL-PUTS keeps trade-off candidates through a Pareto sweep; Primal-Dual Decoding changes pressure through multipliers. Both express preferences. SORT-Gen's selected-item mask blocks duplicates, a distinct feasibility rule. Finite weights allow objectives to compensate for one another, so hard ad-load, inventory, or deduplication constraints need independent checks.

Sources: [A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems](../../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en.md) · [Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems](../../../../reproductions/2607.19357-primal-dual-decoding/README-en.md) · [A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao](../../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en.md)

### The same two-head form does not mean the same control problem

PRL-PUTS estimates Repin/P2P utilities then sweeps policy weights. RLBP heads predict daily BU/CPC change from a production baseline and select PID coefficients, not items. Lower CPC is better, so do not flip a negative lift before subtracting it during fusion. Production gamma=0 uses no cross-day bootstrapping; external beta sets lifecycle trade-offs. Multi-step max/min per head does not guarantee the optimal combined Q. The seven-day A/B and two-month unbalanced holdout need separate interpretation.

Sources: [Reinforcement Learning for Controller Parameters in the Auto-Bidding System at Pinterest](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33248-pinterest-rlbp/README-en.md) · [A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems](../../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en.md)

### A unified slate policy still separates hard constraints from proxy rewards

CDM distills marginal slate supervision from a controlled MMR teacher. OneTrans-GSR instead uses slate RMs to guide one policy that directly generates mixed-content sequences. Its geometric objective first applies group min-max normalization and a positive floor, while rule rewards require separate standardization; it is not arbitrary multiplication of business scores. Hard masks prevent forbidden actions, finite penalties permit trade-offs, and local quotas may conflict. Record RM proxy scores, final selection and real A/B separately rather than relabel CPU arithmetic or predictions on unexposed slates as user gains.

Sources: [OneTrans-GSR: A Generative Slate Ranking Paradigm Unifying Reranking and Mix-Ranking with One Autoregressive Transformer](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.04720-onetrans-gsr/README-en.md) · [Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why shouldn't CDM or SORT-Gen treat an item's standalone CTR as fixed value throughout a slate? {#cross-prefix-changes-marginal-value}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The prefix changes incremental contribution. CDM subtracts redundancy using maximum similarity to the prefix. SORT-Gen predicts cumulative actions conditioned on the prefix to estimate marginal value. Both reject fixed point scores as sufficient for page utility, but whether sacrificing immediate score is worthwhile still requires evaluation.

    **Illustrative example:** The top three videos show the same ski run. A camping clip has a lower independent score but could add more information to a skiing-heavy prefix. That is not a measured CTR gain.

    Sources: [Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en.md) · [A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao](../../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en.md)

### Does keeping a PRL-PUTS Pareto policy mean Repin, P2P, and slate quality all improve? {#cross-pareto-is-not-universal-win}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Nondomination is defined relative to candidate policies and estimated objectives. Repin can improve while P2P declines. SORT-Gen and CDM model a different slate-context level; two-objective nondomination does not guarantee all list metrics improve.

    **Illustrative example:** Policies A=(10,6) and B=(8,9) are both nondominated. Keeping B does not show overall superiority or tell us anything about repeat exposure.

    Sources: [A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems](../../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en.md) · [A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao](../../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en.md) · [Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en.md)

### Why check slate feasibility even when Primal-Dual Decoding raises multipliers dynamically? {#cross-adaptive-weights-not-hard-guarantees}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Multipliers change soft pressure, not whether any feasible combination remains. If early selections rule out a required category, later weighting cannot restore it. SORT-Gen's duplicate mask illustrates hard exclusion versus scoring. PRL-PUTS weight sweeps do not enforce every hard business rule.

    **Illustrative example:** If one position remains and two mutually exclusive categories must be included, no multiplier can satisfy both. Report infeasibility or use a predefined fallback, not just a better total score.

    Sources: [Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems](../../../../reproductions/2607.19357-primal-dual-decoding/README-en.md) · [A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao](../../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en.md) · [A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems](../../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en.md)

### RLBP and PRL-PUTS both have two Q heads and tunable weights. Why are actions and rewards not interchangeable? {#cross-rlbp-two-heads-not-listwise-q}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** PRL-PUTS trades off Repin and P2P in a recommendation policy. RLBP chooses daily PID multipliers to balance budget utilization and CPC. Negative CPC lift is retained, so subtracting beta times Qcpc favors lower cost. Production gamma=0 is a one-step daily objective, not a generic long-horizon slate Q.

    **Illustrative example:** CPC decreasing from 1 to 0.9 gives reward -0.1. Subtracting beta times this value raises the fused score. Flipping it to +0.1 first would penalize lower cost.

    Sources: [Reinforcement Learning for Controller Parameters in the Auto-Bidding System at Pinterest](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.33248-pinterest-rlbp/README-en.md) · [A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems](../../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en.md)

### Does OneTrans-GSR geometric reward guarantee that no objective deteriorates? {#cross-geometric-floor-not-business-guarantee}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Flooring and geometric aggregation change proxy trade-offs, not prove Pareto improvement; a constant objective contributes the same group factor. Actual user effects require independent production A/B, and passing local masks does not prove a jointly feasible completion.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Multiplying normalized click and GMV proxies can still favor a slate overestimated by the RM. A higher CPU formula score is not additional orders.

    Sources: [OneTrans-GSR: A Generative Slate Ranking Paradigm Unifying Reranking and Mix-Ranking with One Autoregressive Transformer](../../../../recommendation-components/2611.04720-onetrans-gsr/README-en.md) · [Contextual Distillation Model for Diversified Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2406.09021-cdm/README-en.md)
